indicators.note: someone holding something has it inside their grasp, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A young woman carries a doctor's instrument, perhaps a stethoscope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor's instrument' reads as one phrase, but the doctor is wordplay and only 'instrument' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a large wooden xylophone, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: A medal on man making explosive

explanation.surface: Pinning a medal on a soldier causes an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonal is a high explosive of ammonium nitrate and aluminium.

indicators.note: an outing is a trip away, so the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: Posh drinks are laid on for a choir's day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outing' reads as a day trip; it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the Greek gods, so a loftily divine liquid.

clue.text: Tedium felt by communist in business upsurge

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other, held between its outer letters

parts.note: a boom is a surge in trade

explanation.surface: A communist finds an economic boom dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weariness of being uninterested, the same as tedium.

explanation.surface: A company draws up a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, but here it is the adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact as an adjective means closely packed and solid; as a noun it is a treaty or pact.

clue.text: Recorded a light blow in one

definitions.note: a phrase for recorded, as in 'got it on tape'

indicators.note: in puts one part inside the other, held between its letters

parts.note: a tap is a gentle knock

explanation.surface: A soft knock was captured on a recording all in one take.
explanation.definitionFit: On tape means captured on magnetic tape, so recorded.

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of material, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A trip to Bootle, a town near Liverpool, results in some dull art.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a work produced merely to earn a living, so routine and uninspired.

clue.text: Fabulous bird upset by lover's blackish-green colour

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, and in a down entry that reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is knocked over by a suitor of a dark green hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbeau, French for crow, names a very dark green that is almost black.

clue.text: He was popularly acclaimed as no other lion, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A man was celebrated as no other lion-hearted hero was.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give HORATIO NELSON, and the whole clue also describes him: a national hero honoured like no other.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson, victor at Trafalgar, was Britain's most popularly acclaimed hero.

parts.note: a cry of surprise or pleasure

explanation.surface: A nurse greets the ward with a cheery cry at the start of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nursemaid or children's nanny in South and East Asia.

indicators.note: something that is giving yields and bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A helicopter's rotor mounting gives the pilot freedom to manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: space to turn round is literal scope for a manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to turn is the space or freedom needed to change direction, so latitude for manoeuvring.

clue.text: Right 'answer returned by editor when trapped

indicators.note: something returned is sent back the way it came, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
ANS is a common abbreviation for answer
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor sends back the right answer after being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Right and answer turn round as one unit before the editor is added. The stray quote mark is in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Snared means caught in a snare, a noose or trap, so trapped.

indicators.note: to cultivate soil is to dig and turn it over, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy hopes to grow a plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is in the scanned clue and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-family flower, in legend the bloom of the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Airline taking a mine over battlefield

parts.note: El Al is Israel's national airline

indicators.note: something turned over is upset and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An air company acquires a mine above an old battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: EL AL, A, then the letters of MINE turned over into MEIN give EL ALAMEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of decisive Second World War battles in 1942.

clue.text: Unusual life-permit to remain temporarily unused

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their ordinary order

explanation.surface: An unusual permit for life lets someone stay idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that lies fallow is left unsown for a season, so it is temporarily unused.

parts.note: f, forte, the musical mark for loud
a lout is an oafish, clumsy fellow

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a noisy country yokel.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout is used loosely as to mock or show scorn for, an older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Light with a tendency to grow less?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slender candle or wick
second meaning: a gradual narrowing towards one end

explanation.surface: A lamp whose brightness keeps fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the second meaning is a playful gloss, and a candle does in fact shrink as it burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle used for lighting, and a taper is also a gradual decrease in width.

clue.text: It is very hard for first male worker

parts.note: Adam, the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: Being the first man employed is a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant, the noun, is a legendary stone of unbreakable hardness.

clue.text: Found her a marshal without precedent

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange troops into order, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Appointing a woman as marshal had never happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' reads as a noun, a rank she is given, but it is the verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard of has never been known before, so it has no precedent.

clue.text: He claims strict rights from former player

explanation.surface: A retired sportsman demands what he is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, demanding payment or rights rigorously.

clue.text: Manage to speak about physical education

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps round the other

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A teacher manages to give a talk on school sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine or business is to run or manage it.

parts.note: do as in 'that will do', to satisfy

explanation.surface: Someone begs another not to sulk when in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite request but is the verb meaning satisfy, as when something will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolour is a literary word for sorrow or grief.

clue.text: Girl finding nothing laid out for dressing

parts.note: Sal, short for Sally or Sarah

indicators.note: laid out means spread out in a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl finds no clothes set out for her to get dressed in.
explanation.walkthrough: SAL, then O with LAID rearranged into ADOIL, gives SALAD OIL. 'Dressing' suggests putting on clothes; it is the salad sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad oil, such as olive oil, is poured over salad as a dressing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Eric ..., the English thriller novelist
second meaning: one who walks at a leisurely pace

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise for a fluent author; it is a famous author's surname and a stroller.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler wrote spy thrillers, and an ambler is someone strolling unhurriedly along.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bowl for holding water
second meaning: an enclosed harbour area

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship moored at a quay; it is a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a wide bowl, and also an enclosed area of water in a harbour where ships moor.

parts.note: surface reading: dismal prospects ahead for someone
setter's reading: a drowsy guard keeps a poor watch, which is also a phrase for dim prospects

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means poor prospects, and a sentry who dozes off is literally keeping a poor watch. The stray quote mark is in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lookout is an idiom for a gloomy outlook, and a lookout is also a guard on watch.

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so these letters are read from the end

explanation.surface: Friends are shocked by a sudden setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like surprise, but it means turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a sharp blow with the open hand.

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged
back tells us to read the preceding word in the opposite direction

parts.note: the word splits as draw plus its back signal

explanation.surface: A manager lists the disadvantages of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning a snag; it splits into DRAW and its turning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages an estate, household or event, acting as its superintendent.

explanation.surface: A royal couple are the more majestic pair.
explanation.walkthrough: GR and ER are royal ciphers seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grander is the comparative of grand, meaning more magnificent or lofty.
